subject: an 18th-century American man with long straight hair worn loose to the shoulders, a broad intelligent face and small round spectacles, wearing a plain brown wool coat, waistcoat and white cravat

panels.01-printshop: a twelve-year-old boy apprentice in a leather apron setting metal type at a wooden composing case in a cramped Boston print shop around 1718, a wooden hand press and hanging printed sheets behind him, window light
panels.02-philadelphia: a tired seventeen-year-old young man in worn travelling clothes walking up a colonial Philadelphia street in 1723 with a large bread roll under each arm, eating a third, brick houses and market stalls, morning light
panels.03-junto: a group of young colonial tradesmen in plain 1720s coats seated around a tavern table at night debating, candles, papers and books on the table, friendly earnest discussion, Philadelphia 1727
panels.04-stove: {S} as a younger man kneeling beside a new cast-iron fireplace stove in a colonial parlour in 1742, examining it, warm glow of the fire, winter frost on the window
panels.05-kite: {S} and a young man in a field beside a wooden shed in 1752 flying a silk kite on a long string toward dark storm clouds, a metal key hanging on the string, wind in the grass, dramatic sky, no lightning strike
panels.06-london: {S} older, standing silent and dignified in a grand wood-panelled council chamber in London in 1774 while a lawyer in a wig speaks against him before seated lords
panels.07-paris: {S} older wearing a fur cap and plain coat, greeted warmly by French courtiers in a gilded Paris salon in 1778, chandeliers, mirrors, elegant 18th-century French clothing
panels.08-abolition: an elderly {S} with thin white hair seated at a desk in Philadelphia in 1790, signing a long handwritten petition with a quill, members of an abolition society standing respectfully around him, candlelight
